notes: Reigned as the sixth king of Babylon's First Dynasty from 1792 to 1750 BCE under the Middle Chronology. He extended Babylonian rule across much of Mesopotamia and is best known for the Code of Hammurabi. Ancient Near Eastern absolute chronology remains disputed; ATLAS uses the Middle Chronology for this record.
Reigned as a pharaoh of Egypt's Nineteenth Dynasty from 1279 to 1213 BCE. He is associated with the Battle of Kadesh, extensive building programs and a reign of about sixty-six years.

Legendary founder and first queen of Carthage. The traditional foundation date is 814 BCE, but her reign and death dates are not historically secure; the same-year end value is a temporary placeholder required by the current schema.
Reigned as king of Macedon from 336 to 323 BCE and led the conquests that overthrew the Achaemenid Empire and created a vast Macedonian empire extending into Egypt and northwestern India.
Served as Carthage's leading commander from 221 BCE and commanded its forces during the Second Punic War, including the invasion of Italy after crossing the Alps. He died in exile around 183 BCE.

Ruled the Ptolemaic Kingdom from 51 to 30 BCE, initially with dynastic co-rulers and later as its dominant sovereign. Her death in 30 BCE marked the end of Ptolemaic rule and preceded Egypt's annexation by Rome.
Seized effective control during the civil war beginning in 49 BCE, held repeated dictatorships, became dictator perpetuo in 44 BCE, and was assassinated on 15 March of that year.
King of the Catuvellauni and a dominant ruler in southeastern Britain. His reign is conventionally dated approximately from 9 to 40 CE based on coinage and Roman literary evidence.
Queen of the Iceni who led a major uprising against Roman rule in Britain in 60–61 CE. Her forces destroyed Camulodunum, Londinium and Verulamium before the revolt was defeated.
Reigned as Roman emperor from 306 to 337. He became sole ruler of the Roman Empire in 324 and founded Constantinople as an imperial capital.

Reigned as Byzantine emperor from 527 to 565. His reign is associated with the Corpus Juris Civilis, major building projects including Hagia Sophia, and campaigns that restored imperial rule over parts of the western Mediterranean.
Served as a leading Byzantine general during the reign of Justinian I, commanding campaigns against the Sasanian Empire, the Vandal Kingdom and the Ostrogothic Kingdom.

Founded the Wu Zhou dynasty and ruled China as emperor from 690 until her abdication in 705. She had exercised substantial political authority before formally taking the throne, but this timeline record uses her sovereign reign as the map-display period.
Founded the Mongol Empire and ruled as its first khagan from 1206 until his death in 1227, unifying the Mongol tribes and launching major campaigns across Eurasia.
Served as the ninth Huey Tlatoani of the Aztec Empire from 1502 until his death in 1520 during the Spanish conquest led by Hernán Cortés.
Reigned as queen of England and Ireland from 1558 until her death in 1603 and was the last monarch of the Tudor dynasty.
Passed the military examination and entered government service in 1576; served as Joseon's leading naval commander and was killed at the Battle of Noryang in 1598.
Served as the first shogun of the Tokugawa Shogunate from 1603 until his formal abdication in 1605.

role: Retired shogun and de facto ruler
notes: Continued to exercise decisive political authority as retired shogun from 1605 until his death in 1616.
Reigned as king of Prussia from 1740 until his death in 1786 and transformed Prussia into a major European power through war, territorial expansion and state reform.
Reigned as king of the Zulu from 1816 until his assassination in 1828 and expanded the Zulu polity through military and administrative reorganization.
Reigned as Emperor of the French from 1804 until his first abdication in 1814.
Returned from exile and ruled again during the Hundred Days in 1815 before his final abdication.
Served as the sixteenth president of the United States from 1861 until his assassination in 1865, leading the Union through the American Civil War.

role: Political leader and independence movement leader
notes: Returned to India in 1915 and became the leading figure of the Indian independence movement through mass civil resistance and nonviolent political campaigns. He remained politically active until his assassination in 1948.

role: General Secretary and de facto leader
notes: Became the dominant leader of the Soviet Union after Lenin's death in 1924 and ruled until his own death in 1953. By the mid-1930s he had eliminated major political opposition and exercised dictatorial control over party and state.
Founding leader of the People's Republic of China who exercised paramount political authority from its establishment in 1949 until his death in 1976.
